text:
Mira Patel: Heads up — during preflight on the onprem cluster (edge-zone-3) I saw unexpected outbound connections from sealed-node-27 to a third-party telemetry IP. Saw a KMS decrypt error in the agent logs right after. Is this a vuln or a misconfig from last night's RBAC PR? :eyes:

Ryan Chen: thanks Mira. Can you paste the agent logs + exact timestamps? tagging @Sam Ortega for RBAC/audit.

Mira Patel: pasted logs:
```json
{ "ts": "2026-03-21T03:12:10Z", "msg": "kms/decrypt failed: access denied", "svc": "keystore-agent", "node": "sealed-node-27", "dst": "34.77.12.99:443" }
```
Also PR 4823 landed last night — removed legacy svcacc role binding.

Sam Ortega: ack. This smells like least-privilege regressed. Did PR 4823 remove a service-account binding used by the keystore shim? @Kevin Liu any oncall context? :thinking_face:

Kevin Liu: I'm on it. Running quick check: `kubectl -n sealed get rolebinding | grep keystore` ... nothing for agent-sa on that node's ns. I also see audit logs show `TokenReview` for agent-sa rejected at 03:12:09.

Mira Patel: we also have network policy that should prevent egress, but sealed-node-27 is on legacy vlan. I suspect both RBAC and netpol gaps.

security-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0319-09 — 'onprem sealed-node outbound + KMS decrypt fail'. Severity: high. Paging oncall. :rotating_light:

Ryan Chen: Triage plan: 1) isolate node (cordon + evict), 2) rotate agent credentials (ephemeral), 3) reapply audit-aware RBAC bindings, 4) block egress subnet from that VLAN via firewall, 5) collect forensic logs and preserve PVs.

Kevin Liu: running commands now:
```
kubectl cordon sealed-node-27
kubectl drain sealed-node-27 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
kubectl -n sealed delete secret agent-creds-sealed-node-27
```
Will also attach pcap from host: /var/log/pcap/20260321-0312.pcap.gz

Sam Ortega: Forensics note — if the agent attempted KMS decrypt and failed, there may be a dangling retry loop leaking tokens; check for repeated TokenReview calls. Also confirm KMS audit logs for decrypt rejects and caller identity.

Mira Patel: pulling KMS audit: `kms-audit-20260321.log` shows `DecryptRequest` from `project:sealed-node-27@svc` denied with `principal:agent-sa` — audit payload includes request headers that show no x-goog-credential header.

Kevin Liu: Temporarily rebind agent-sa with least privilege:
```
kubectl -n sealed apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: keystore-agent-binding-temp
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: agent-sa
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: keystore-agent-role
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
EOF
```

Sam Ortega: Good. Also add audit annotation `incident=INC-2026-0319-09` to the RoleBinding for traceability. We'll revert after root cause. :lock:

Mira Patel: After rebind, keystore-agent logs show decrypt success at 03:15:02 and no further outbound traffic. Reattached pcap to thread.

Ryan Chen: Next steps: - file a follow-up PR to reintroduce the RBAC test in CI, - add netpol egress deny-by-default for legacy vlan namespaces, - schedule tabletop on verifying KMS audit alert thresholds.

Kevin Liu: I've left the node cordoned and created a snapshot: `gcloud compute disks snapshot ...` — snapshot id: snap-20260321-sealed27. Will keep secrets rotated and secret removed from node's disk.

Mira Patel: One more ask — can infra add a rule to block known telemetry IPs at perimeter until we confirm it's benign? 34.77.12.99 flagged by ThreatIntel.

Ryan Chen: I'll open firewall ticket and add temporary deny for that IP for that VLAN. Also tagging @InfraChange for emergency change. :white_check_mark:

OpsRunbook: Logged all actions to incident playbook: https://intranet.redwood/ops/incidents/INC-2026-0319-09 — follow checklist 'onprem-keystore-incident'

Sam Ortega: After action: schedule RBAC rollback proof and a red-team sim to validate no further silent egress. Closing loop by 2026-03-25 EOD. :wave:
